problem:
Find the distance between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -2 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}5 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}9 & 3 \\ 3 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-17 \\ -14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{15}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-17 \\ -14\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(5-3)^{2}+(5-6)^{2}+(1-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+1} \\  & =\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
